located_point.method: Approximate. Dales and Kenoyer 1977 Fig. 3 prints the site coordinates '66° 42' 30" E. Long.' and '25° 27' 45" N. LAT.' (25.4625 N, 66.7083 E), 30 m from the infrastructure starting point. Renders at 2 km and 800 m (RGB, SWIR) show only irrigated field patches and tracks there; the mound could not be distinguished.

imagery_unmeasurable_reason: Features not resolvable at 10 m: the mound is not distinguishable among field patches, and the excavated rooms are 2-6 m across.

sources.rights_notice: Copernicus Sentinel data terms; Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2018–2026
sources.status: used for location only; no line measured

sources.citation: George F. Dales and Jonathan Mark Kenoyer 1977, 'Shell Working at Ancient Balakot, Pakistan', Expedition 19(2): 13-19, University Museum, University of Pennsylvania. Plan library entry balakot-02 (publisher PDF)
sources.figure: Fig. 4, 'Plan of excavated portion of the high mount that dominates the western half of the site. Structures of the Harrappan levels.'
sources.north_evidence: Thin arrow with a solid head and 'N' above it, lower left of the plan; no meaning stated.

notes: Eighteen wall faces were measured on Fig. 4 in three building groups. The eastern group lies between 0.0 and +3.0 degrees from the plan's arrow; the central building's long walls between +7.1 and +10.3 degrees, with its south wall at +1.7 and +5.6 (one face each); the western building is not rectangular as drawn: its north wall runs at +5.8, its east wall at -0.8 and its south room wall at 0.0. Systems are the greedy 6 degree windows of scripts-S/group.py: the main window (-0.03 to +5.97) collects the eastern group, the western building's north and south walls and the central building's south wall. The central building alone would give about +8.6. Fig. 3 (whole site) has its own N arrow and the note 'Based on Pakistan Arch. Dept. Survey 1962', but shows excavation areas only as filled blocks; we did not measure it.
